text.p: These are the main stories in Estonian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hopes to sign a border deal with Russia at the Lisbon OSCE summit were not realised. The agreement may be signed during a visit of Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeni Primakov to Tallinn in January.
- Prosecutors have demanded the death penalty for a man who killed a police officer in April.
- President Lennart Meri wants explanations for recent incidents involving the Defence League, a volunteer homeguard which is part of the state defence system.

- The new chairman of the Democratic Labour Party, the party that was formed from the old Communist party of Estonia, refuses to call himself a former Communist and predicts that his party will gain seats in the next parliament.
- Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi promised to discuss with the new economy minister the possibility of cutting income tax for companies.
- Parliament's Russian faction, which is composed of two Russian parties, are to discuss the row which has threatened to split them.
- Estonia is to continue talks with the WTO in December and February and expects to join it in the spring, foreign ministry vice-chancellor Priit Kolbre said.
- The decision to improve the weapons of the four Estonian infantry battalions has raised the interest of defence firms to Estonia, a defence ministry official said.
- IMF resident representative Basil Zavoico said that starting protective tariffs would protect inefficient branches of the Estonian economy.
